concerns.text: The plan conditions mediation on having ≥ 50 measured‑stress rows but provides no a priori power analysis to justify that threshold. Without a power calculation, it is unclear whether the sample will be sufficient to detect a meaningful indirect effect, risking inconclusive results.

Residual‑stress proxy values are used in Feature Set C and in predictive comparisons, yet the plan does not address the construct validity of this proxy. Mixing proxy‑derived stress with measured stress may confound interpretation of any performance gain attributed to “stress‑mediated” features.

Mediation analysis is performed on observational data. Even though the document states that findings will be labeled ‘associational’, the use of mediation terminology (a‑path, b‑path, indirect effect) implies a causal pathway and may be misinterpreted. A more appropriate analysis (e.g., structural equation modeling with explicit causal assumptions) or clearer framing is needed.

The mediation models control for “all other covariates” but the plan does not specify which covariates are included beyond material class. Without explicit confounder selection, omitted variable bias could invalidate the indirect‑effect estimates.

ΔMAPE is reported as a performance drop when training on one material and testing on another, but no statistical test (e.g., permutation test) is proposed to assess whether the observed drop is significant. This limits the ability to draw robust conclusions about cross‑material generalization.
